scope: Read-only static follow-up of the installed Rust client trusted player-count request, cache retention, and Nexus exemption. No game process or memory access, client edits, account/session operations, backend writes, service startup, or tests were performed.
addressConvention: All native addresses are GameAssembly.dll RVAs; image base 0x180000000.

construction.finding: Concatenates the platform API base and relative endpoint, then passes URL and callback to a shared download wrapper. The live configured base was not read.

httpWrapper.finding: Creates a UnityWebRequest.Get for the URL, creates DownloadStringCoroutine(request, callback), and starts the coroutine. A localhost HTTPS-to-HTTP rewrite exists; this is not evidence of production redirection.

downloadCoroutine.finding: Yields the send operation, checks result against integer 2 for logging, then reads download-handler text and invokes the callback; the request is disposed afterward. The error logging branch does not itself skip the callback.

requestPath.credentialsObservation: No SteamID, game-session ticket, account identifier, custom authentication header, or cache-busting parameter was found on this recovered URL-plus-callback request path. This does not characterize all Unity/native HTTP behavior.

oneMinuteThreshold.finding: The ordinary browser path passes false and returns before initiating another update if the elapsed interval is less than one minute. This is a minimum request interval, not an automatic one-minute refresh timer or a map TTL.

attemptTimestamp.finding: The timestamp is stored directly after starting the asynchronous request, before the response callback. Empty or malformed responses can therefore still consume the one-minute request interval.

emptyResponse.finding: Null or empty response text does not enter the parser and does not clear the existing shared map.

replacementMap.finding: Builds a replacement endpoint-to-integer map and publishes it after iteration. JSON deserialization or pre-publication exceptions can retain the previous map. Individually unparseable endpoint keys are skipped rather than necessarily failing the entire response.

requestThrottleAndMapRetention.expirationLimit: No independent age-based invalidation of the map was established on the recovered request/callback/apply path. This is not a claim that every caller or native HTTP cache was inspected.

nonemptyMapMissingTarget.finding: Uses zero for the finite cap when the map is nonempty but the target IP plus ConnectionPort has no entry.

mapApplication.mapHit: Passes the map integer to a cloned server model. The constructor parses tags, then stores max(0, min(PlayersAfterTags, mapCount)).
mapApplication.fixedFiveFinding: No fixed cap of five was recovered in this relevant request-to-model chain. A fresh map value of five is sufficient to limit an otherwise higher model count to five.

nexusExemption.finding: The skip condition in the browser trusted-count apply loop is the Nexus identity condition: a nonnull NexusEndpoint and a positive unsigned NexusId. It is not a special case for five players.

browserChecks.operation: Check model pointer at +0x78 against null
Check model integer at +0xd8 against zero
Unsigned-above branch skips applying trusted-count clone

installedClientConstructor.endpointArgument: Third managed constructor argument in R9, retained in RSI. Validates nonnull/non-whitespace, then stores at +0x78 at RVA 0xca91421.
installedClientConstructor.nexusIdArgument: Fourth managed constructor argument, loaded from frame+0x50 at RVA 0xca913ae; rejects <=0 at 0xca913b5 and stores at +0xd8 at 0xca91489.

selectedExceptionLiteralEvidence.literal: Nexus ID must be greater than 0

tagCrossCheck.finding: The nexuszone tag sets the zone flag to the negation of the same endpoint-plus-id condition, matching the readable local server-copy IsNexus/IsNexusZone semantics.

localReadableCrossCheck.limitation: The local server copy supplies readable semantic cross-checks; the installed client native stores and preserved exception strings provide the direct field identification. The local copy is not the running remote server.

nexusExemption.targetClassificationLimit: This static result does not establish whether the current remote target is Nexus. Its current server model/tags were not sampled by this follow-up.

normalClientDisconnectComparison.purpose: Compare ordinary-client admission with backend count publication while independent research sessions stay unchanged; separate an externally published value from a possible retained local map.
suggestedSequence: Record a synchronized baseline: target public-feed count and batch marker, A2S players/cp, exact-target Steam count, independently connected session state, and normal-client browser display.
Have the user normally disconnect only the already-running ordinary Rust client. Do not stop independent research sessions or change server configuration.
Observe at least two distinct new public-feed batch markers. Six elapsed minutes may capture only one new batch, depending on start alignment; backend accounting delay remains unknown.
Record a normal reconnect, repeat the same synchronized observations through at least two new backend batches, and compare both directions.
If server administration is available, record authoritative active/awake/sleeping counts and join/leave times to account for unrelated player activity.
canSupport: A repeatable decrement after normal disconnection and increment after normal reconnection, with other players controlled, supports that this client contributes to that published statistic.

The actual ordinary-client HTTP response or a suitably scoped existing client log is needed to identify which map the browser consumed; a separately fetched public response alone does not prove the UI used that batch.
cannotEstablish: An unchanged count alone does not prove research accounts were excluded, blacklisted, banned, or rejected by EAC, nor identify the backend algorithm.
Six minutes alone does not establish a definitive maximum publication delay.
Other player changes and unknown aggregation or publication delays can confound a single disconnect comparison.

privacy: No credentials, tokens, tickets, account/player/entity IDs, coordinates, full symbol/string tables, or raw network payloads are included.
